title: Partial algebraization preserving a marking and prime-to-ell degree
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime and let $X$ be a normal complete local Noetherian scheme of dimension $d\geq2$ on which $\ell$ is invertible. Let $Z\subset X$ be a nowhere dense closed subset. There are a normal complete local integral Noetherian scheme $X^+$, a finite surjective morphism $p:X^+\to X$ whose extension of function fields has degree prime to $\ell$, a complete regular local excellent Noetherian scheme $Y_0$ of dimension $d-1$, an integral affine excellent Noetherian scheme $W$ with a dominant finite-type morphism $f_0:W\to Y_0$ having fibres of dimension at most one and generic fibre of dimension one, a closed point $w\in W$ above the closed point of $Y_0$, and a nowhere dense closed subset $Z_W\subset W$, such that the completion morphism $g:X^+\to W$ at $w$ identifies $X^+$ with $\operatorname{Spec}\widehat{\mathcal O_{W,w}}$ and $p^{-1}Z=g^{-1}Z_W$. The scheme $W$ can be chosen normal. The morphism $g$ is regular, meaning flat with geometrically regular fibres. The prime $\ell$ is invertible on $Y_0$ and $W$. In equal characteristic $p$ can be the identity. Completion is for powers of the maximal ideal; normal means having integrally closed local domains; geometric regularity means regularity after all finite residue-field extensions.

The notions used here are [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-exc-excellent-ring], [def-weil-regular-scheme], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], [def-weil-flat-morphism].

source.place: Expose V 2.1.2 and 3.1.1--3.1.4, printed pp. 64--66, in the geometric form used in IX 1.3, p. 132. Shrink about the algebraization point to the relative-curve locus; excellence makes its completion map regular, and normality descends from the faithfully flat normal completed local ring and spreads near that point.

proof.text: Write $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and choose an ideal $I\subseteq A$ with $Z=V(I)$. Apply [lem-per-prime-to-ell-equivariant-cohen-presentation] to $A,\ell$, obtaining $B,H,V,r$ and $A^+=B^H$. Put $X^+=\operatorname{Spec}A^+$. The map $A\hookrightarrow A^+$ is module-finite, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral] and [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-lying-over] give a finite surjection $p:X^+\to X$. The function-field degree is prime to $\ell$ by the presentation. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-complete-local-product], the finite domain $A^+$ is Noetherian complete local. It is normal: an element of $\operatorname{Frac}(B^H)$ integral over $B^H$ is integral over $B$, hence belongs to $B$ by normality; being a fraction of invariant elements, it is fixed by $H$, hence belongs to $B^H$. In equal characteristic $A^+=A$ and $p$ is the identity.

Apply [lem-per-equivariant-marked-cylinder-algebraization] to this formal presentation and the single ideal $I^+=IA^+$. Its hypotheses hold: $H$ has invertible order in $V$, fixes the variables, and the finite map is etale away from an element nonzero on the coefficient special fibre. Obtain coordinates $u_i$, $D=V^H[[u_1,\ldots,u_{r-1}]]$, a quasi-finite $D[T]$-algebra $C$, a maximal $\mathfrak n$ over $(\mathfrak m_D,T)$, and an ideal $J\subset C$, with $\widehat{C_{\mathfrak n}}\cong A^+$ carrying $J\widehat{C_{\mathfrak n}}$ onto $I^+$. The formal-presentation node gives that $D$ is complete regular Noetherian local of dimension $d-1$: in equal characteristic $r=d$, and in mixed characteristic $r=d-1$ over a DVR. It also gives that $\ell$ is a unit in $D$.

The ring $D$ is excellent by [lem-per-complete-local-excellence]. Finite-type and localization permanence [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent] make $C$ and $L=C_{\mathfrak n}$ excellent and Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat] the map $L\to A^+=\widehat L$ is faithfully flat. Ideal contraction [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction], applied to the zero ideal, embeds $L$ in the domain $A^+$. If $a/b\in\operatorname{Frac}L$ is integral over $L$, its image in $\operatorname{Frac}(A^+)$ is integral over $A^+$, hence lies in $A^+$. Thus $a\in bA^+$. Contraction for the principal ideal $bL$ gives $a\in bL$, so $a/b\in L$. Consequently $L$ is a normal domain. This is the faithfully-flat normality-descent argument written out for the particular local domains.

The kernel $K$ of $C\to C_{\mathfrak n}$ is finitely generated, since $C$ is Noetherian. For each of a finite set of generators $k_j$, choose $s_j\notin\mathfrak n$ with $s_jk_j=0$, using the definition of localization. Set $s=\prod_j s_j$ (or $1$ if the kernel is zero). Then $s\notin\mathfrak n$ and $C_s\to C_{\mathfrak n}$ is injective: a fraction in its kernel has numerator in $K$, annihilated by $s$. Thus $C_s$ is a domain. Replacing $C,J,\mathfrak n$ by their localizations at $s$ leaves $L$, its completion, and the extended ideal $I^+$ unchanged. It preserves finite type over $D$ and quasi-finiteness over $D[T]$: an open restriction just removes points from each finite fibre.

The integral affine Noetherian scheme $\operatorname{Spec}C$ is excellent in the sense of [lem-per-excellent-normalization-preparation]: for an affine open $V\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}C$, the open immersion $V\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ is locally of finite type between affine schemes, so $\mathcal O(V)$ is a finite type $C$-algebra, excellent by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent]. Apply [lem-per-excellent-normalization-preparation] to $\operatorname{Spec}C$. It has a dense open $U$ isomorphic to an open of its normal normalization. Choose a nonempty principal open $D(h)\subseteq U$. Its coordinate ring $C_h$ is a normal domain: it is the ring of an affine open in a normal integral scheme. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-normal-locus-open] makes the normal locus of $C$ open. It contains $\mathfrak n$ by Step 3. Choose $t\notin\mathfrak n$ with $D(t)$ in this locus, and replace $C$ by $R=C_t$ and $J$ by $JR$. Put $W=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $Y_0=\operatorname{Spec}D$, $w=\mathfrak nR$ and $Z_W=V(JR)$. The scheme $W$ is normal integral affine excellent Noetherian; its local ring at $w$ is still $L$, so $X^+=\operatorname{Spec}\widehat{\mathcal O_{W,w}}$.

The composite $D\to R\to L\to A^+$ is the injective formal-coordinate inclusion of Step 2. Therefore $D\to R$ is injective, so $f_0:W\to Y_0$ is dominant. It is finite type since $R$ was obtained from a finite-type $D$-algebra by two principal localizations. The point $w$ remains maximal, with finite residue field over $D/\mathfrak m_D$, and lies over the closed point of $Y_0$. Since $\ell$ is already a unit in $D$, its image is a unit in $R$.

The morphism $W\to\mathbf A^1_D$ furnished by $D[T]\to R$ is locally quasi-finite. By [lem-weil-pbc-separated-lqf-base-change], for each $y\in Y_0$ its base change $W_y\to\mathbf A^1_{\kappa(y)}$ is locally quasi-finite. It is an affine finite-type map, so the corresponding ring map is quasi-finite at every prime. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-quasi-finite-over-polynomial-algebra] with the field $\kappa(y)$ and one variable. It gives $\dim W_y\leq1$ (including empty fibres).

We check that the generic fibre has dimension exactly one. By [lem-weil-pbc-completion-dimension], $\dim L=\dim A^+$. The finite integral injection $A\to A^+$ gives $\dim A^+=d$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral, lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-dimension-equal]. Apply [lem-exc-dimension-formula-universally-catenary-finite-type-domain] to $D\subset R$ at the maximal point $w$ over $\mathfrak m_D$. Excellence makes $D$ universally catenary; $\operatorname{ht}(w)=d$, $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak m_D)=d-1$, and the residue extension is finite, hence has transcendence degree zero. The formula therefore gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\operatorname{Frac}D}\operatorname{Frac}R=1$. The generic fibre has coordinate ring $R\otimes_D\operatorname{Frac}D$, an integral finite-type algebra over a field, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-domain-dimension-trdeg] gives dimension one.

Since $L$ is excellent, it is a G-ring. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-g-ring-completion-regular] gives a regular ring map $L\to\widehat L=A^+$. The map $R\to L$ is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-regular]. The fibre of $R\to A^+$ over a prime $\mathfrak q\subset R$ is zero if $\mathfrak q\not\subseteq w$, since some element of $\mathfrak q\setminus w$ is inverted in $L$. If $\mathfrak q\subseteq w$, it is the fibre of $L\to A^+$ at $\mathfrak qL$, whose residue field is $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$. These fibres are Noetherian by the completion node (and trivially for the zero ring). Hence [lem-weil-pbc-regular-composition] applies and shows that $R\to A^+$ is regular. Its spectrum map is precisely the canonical completion morphism $g:X^+\to W$.

Under $\widehat L\cong A^+$ we have $JR\cdot A^+=IA^+$, so inverse images of closed sets give $g^{-1}Z_W=V(IA^+)=p^{-1}Z$. Moreover $Z_W$ is nowhere dense. Since $X$ is integral and $V(I)$ is nowhere dense, $I$ contains a nonzero element (also when $I=A$, corresponding to empty $Z$). Injectivity $A\to A^+$ makes $IA^+\ne0$, hence $JR\ne0$. A nonzero ideal in the domain $R$ does not contain the generic point in its zero set, so $V(JR)$ is nowhere dense. This proves all clauses.
